newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq composite closes down more than two percent.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq composite closes down more than two percent.

text.p: Nasdaq shares dropped more than two percent amid a sharp decline in technology stocks and escalating fears of interest rate hikes, traders said.
The Nasdaq composite index shed 28.87 points or 2.34 percent to close unofficially at 1206.90.
The Dow industrials sank 148 points to 6391.
Stronger-than-expected producer price data released Friday morning convinced many investors that the Federal Reserve could further tighten interest rates, analysts said.

"There's no real panic in the market, but it's an insidious slide and the sell pressure remains on. The PPI numbers and the revised retail sales figures could be seen as a bit inflationary, so that didn't help things," said Jack Bayer, a managing director at Oppenheimer & Co. Retail sales figures for January and February were revised upward.
Intel Corp lead the Nasdaq decline, falling 6-3/4 to 130-1/2. The company reports its earnings on Monday.
Computer networking stocks also sank after Cascade Communications Corp reported disappointing quarterly results, which were released after the market closed Thursday.
Declining issues beat advancing issues 3058 to 1268 on total volume of 545 million shares.
